regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8%; PMI 56.5","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% is the headline; the quality check fails on two counts. PMI Composite slipped to 56.5 from 58.9 — still expansionary, but the direction matters — and core sector growth at 2.3% YoY (down from 4.7%) is the lowest in 18 months, signalling that the physical economy is decelerating even as the statistical one flatters. Invert the growth story: if airline passenger traffic has fallen to a 7th-percentile 35.08 mn and e-commerce GMV growth has halved to 12.4% from 25%, the 7.8% print is carrying more statistical weight than ground-level velocity warrants.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 3.21%; Fuel -3.78%%","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 3.21% is benign — but it is moving in the wrong direction, up from 2.75% prior, driven by food inflation at 3.47% (up from 2.13%). Core CPI is flat at 3.4%, which tells you the food spike is not yet feeding through — but Brent at $96.28, up from $88.10 six months ago, will push fuel CPI from -3.78% into positive territory within 60 days, and the RBI has already revised its own inflation forecast to 4.6% from 4.2%. A rate cut priced by the market is a rate cut the data does not yet support.","badge_label":"Within Band","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 13.8%; CD 83.04%","signal_text":"CD ratio at 83.04% — an 81st-percentile reading — with credit growing at 13.8% against deposits at 10.8% is a 300bps structural gap that the system cannot sustain without either deposit rate wars or regulatory intervention. NBFC credit growth has already decelerated from 17% to 13% — the canary in the wholesale funding mine — while corporate bond issuance surged to ₹1,12,000 cr, a 7th-percentile print, as firms front-run tighter conditions. Last time India's CD ratio sustained above 80% during an easing cycle was FY14; within 12 months, the taper tantrum forced an emergency reversal — the setup rhymes, even if FX reserves at current levels provide more runway.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25%%","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% is unchanged, and with RBI's own inflation forecast at 4.6%, the real rate is approximately 105bps — positive but thin. A Brent-driven CPI overshoot above 4% would compress that buffer to near zero, making any near-term cut politically difficult to defend. For housing, the average home loan rate has already eased to 8.32% from 8.82% — but with the affordability index at a 19th-percentile 3.5, transmission is not reaching the mass-market buyer.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 12.5%%; CU Not available in search results%","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 12.5% YoY — up sharply from 4.3% prior — is the most encouraging number in today's data set, but it sits in direct contradiction with core sector growth at 2.3%. Capital goods production and core sector output (cement, steel, electricity, coal) should move together if investment is genuinely accelerating; when they diverge this sharply, the IIP print is likely reflecting a single large order or base-effect arithmetic rather than a broad capex revival. Without capacity utilisation data to anchor the read, the prudent call is to treat the 12.5% as a data point, not a trend.","badge_label":"Steady Investment","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST 200640; PV 26.1%","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,00,640 cr — an 84th-percentile YTD reading — is the strongest consumption signal in today's data, but the composition matters more than the headline. PV sales at +26.1% and two-wheeler sales at +28.68% confirm that discretionary spending is accelerating at the upper end of the income distribution; retail mall vacancy collapsing to 6.7% (from 8.3%) — filled by premium F&B and experiential retail, not mass-market apparel — reinforces the same bifurcation. E-commerce GMV growth halving to 12.4% from 25% is the counter-signal: the mass-market digital consumer is pulling back precisely where the affluent physical consumer is accelerating.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 13.8% YoY vastly outpaces deposit growth at 10.8% YoY, widening the CD ratio to 83.04% — now at the 81st percentile, a 3-year high. This 300bps divergence signals funding stress. NBFC credit growth has already decelerated from 17% to 13%, a leading indicator of wholesale funding pressure. Corporate bond issuance surged to ₹112,000 cr (vs ₹106,000 cr prior), the 7th percentile — firms are front-running a tightening cycle.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios >45% and retail deposit franchises; they will poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities — margin compression is imminent. Expect RBI to signal rate cuts in Q2 to ease deposit pressure, but only after credit growth moderates. Position for a 50bps cut by June.","pct_10y":81,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 81st percentile has historically preceded either deposit acceleration or credit slowdown within 2-3 months. Last time it was this high (2022), RBI cut rates 40bps within 60 days.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"watch","title":"Capex Momentum Stalls, Demand Divergence Widens","data_text":"IIP capital goods growth at 12.5% YoY (up from 4.3% prior) masks a deeper slowdown: core sector growth collapsed to 2.3% YoY from 4.7%, the lowest in 18 months. Capacity utilisation data unavailable, but order book proxies (airline passenger traffic down 86% to 35.08 YoY, e-commerce GMV growth halved to 12.4% from 25%) suggest demand is rolling over. GST collections remain strong at ₹200,640 cr YoY, but this reflects consumption, not capex.","implication":"Capex cycle is peaking, not accelerating. Avoid cyclical capex plays (cement, steel, heavy equipment) — order books will compress in Q2. Rotate into defensive consumption (FMCG, pharma) and services (IT, telecom). Public capex remains steady, but private capex is decelerating; watch for government to front-load infrastructure spending to offset.","pct_10y":48,"pct_note":"Core sector at 2.3% is at the 48th percentile — historically, readings below 3% have preceded 2-3 quarters of capex underperformance. This is a yellow flag, not a red one.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Accounts Surge, But Ticket Size Inflates","data_text":"SIP inflows remain robust at ₹29,845 cr (85th percentile), but SIP accounts grew only 1.55% to 10.45 cr while SIP AUM jumped 1.71% to ₹16.64 tr. This divergence — AUM growth outpacing account growth — signals affluent money entering, not mass retail. Equity MF net inflows at ₹25,978 cr (65th percentile) confirm broad-based appetite. MF AUM at ₹82.03 tr (80th percentile) is at a 10-year high.","implication":"This is late-cycle retail behaviour. Affluent investors are rotating into equities; mass retail is still cautious. Overweight large-cap, quality-focused funds and avoid micro-cap/small-cap plays that rely on retail momentum. SIP growth will likely decelerate as the market corrects — prepare for a 15-20% equity MF inflow slowdown if Nifty falls 8-10%.","pct_10y":85,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 85th percentile have historically peaked 3-4 months before equity market corrections. The last time SIP AUM growth exceeded account growth this sharply was in early 2021, preceding a 25% correction.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Oil Rally Threatens Inflation, CAD Widens","data_text":"Brent crude surged to $96.28/bbl (68th percentile), up from $88.10 six months ago — a 9.3% rally. WTI at $91.48 (77th percentile) confirms the move. Copper at 6.68 (80th percentile) and iron ore at 161.91 (63rd percentile) signal broad commodity strength. India's fuel inflation is currently -3.78%, but this is a lagging indicator; a sustained $95+ Brent will push fuel CPI positive within 60 days, risking headline inflation above 4%.","implication":"Current account deficit will widen by 30-40bps if Brent stays above $95 for 2+ quarters. RBI will be forced to defend the INR more aggressively, limiting rate cuts. Hedge long India equity exposure with short oil or long USD. Overweight energy stocks (ONGC, Reliance) as they benefit from higher crude, but avoid refiners (IOC, HPCL) with weak hedges.","pct_10y":68,"pct_note":"Brent at 68th percentile with upward momentum has historically preceded 2-3 quarters of CAD pressure. In 2022, a similar rally led to a 100bps widening of the CAD within 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"watch","title":"Fed Pause Masks Divergence, Carry Unwind Risk","data_text":"Fed funds rate flat at 3.63% (67th percentile), but US 10Y Treasury yields at 4.77% (86th percentile) signal market pricing of higher-for-longer rates. Fed balance sheet contracting at $6.74tr (47th percentile) — QT continues. ECB at 2% deposit rate (flat), BOJ at 0.75% (flat). DXY at 99.15 (46th percentile) is stable, but US equity strength (S&P 500 at 100th percentile, Nasdaq at 72nd) is masking carry trade fragility. US VIX at 14.53 (8th percentile) — complacency is extreme.","implication":"Carry trades are crowded; any Fed hawkish surprise or US equity correction will trigger rapid unwinding. This will weaken emerging market currencies (INR, BRL, MXN) and force RBI to intervene. Position for a 2-3% INR depreciation if US yields spike above 5%. Reduce leverage in EM carry trades; the risk/reward is unfavourable. Overweight USD-denominated assets and underweight INR-hedged EM exposure.","pct_10y":86,"pct_note":"US 10Y at 86th percentile with VIX at 8th percentile is a classic divergence — historically, this has preceded a 15-20% equity correction within 2-3 months as volatility normalizes.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"positive","title":"INR Stabilizes, RBI Reserves Adequate","data_text":"INR/USD at 94.34 (87th percentile), down from 96.15 six months ago — a 1.9% appreciation. FII equity flows turned negative at -₹114 cr (49th percentile), but this is offset by DII inflows at ₹128 cr (22nd percentile). India's household debt at 42.6% of GDP (51st percentile) is manageable vs US at 68% (36th percentile). RBI's inflation forecast at 4.6% (vs 4.2% prior) signals confidence in price stability.","implication":"INR strength is structural, not cyclical — driven by domestic growth and RBI's credibility. FII outflows are temporary (global liquidity concerns), not a sign of India weakness. Maintain INR exposure; the currency is a hedge against global volatility. Avoid hedging INR for 12+ month horizons — the rupee will likely trade 93-95 by year-end. Overweight India equities for foreign investors; INR appreciation is a bonus return.","pct_10y":87,"pct_note":"INR at 87th percentile strength has historically been sustained for 4-6 quarters when driven by growth differentials (India 7.8% vs US 1.5%). Last similar episode was 2016-2017, when INR appreciated 8% over 18 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Retail Mall Recovery Signals Affluent Consumption Shift","data_text":"Retail mall vacancy collapsed to 6.7% (15th percentile, 70th signal score) from 8.3% — the sharpest 6-month tightening in 3 years. Simultaneously, office absorption surged to 26.9 mn sqft (21st percentile, -58 signal score) while office vacancy fell to 14.5%. This divergence is non-obvious: office space is being absorbed by GCCs (Google, Microsoft, Accenture), not traditional IT services. Retail malls are being filled by premium F&B and experiential retail, not mass-market apparel. PV sales +26.1% YoY and 2W sales +28.68% YoY confirm affluent discretionary spending is accelerating.","implication":"The consumption story is bifurcating: mass retail is slowing (e-commerce GMV growth halved to 12.4%), but affluent consumption is accelerating (mall rents in Mumbai +6% to ₹125, Bengaluru +7% to ₹100.6). This is a late-cycle signal. Overweight premium retail REITs (Brookfield, Embassy) and luxury consumption plays (premium auto, high-end hospitality). Underweight mass-market retail and e-commerce. The affluent consumer will sustain growth for 2-3 more quarters, but mass retail weakness will eventually drag overall consumption. Hedge with short positions in mass-market e-commerce and discount retail.","pct_10y":15,"pct_note":"Retail mall vacancy at 15th percentile (tightest in 10 years) combined with office absorption at 21st percentile has historically preceded 2-3 quarters of premium real estate outperformance, followed by a sharp correction as the cycle peaks. In 2019, a similar pattern preceded a 30% REIT correction in 2020.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP growth with a PMI Composite at 56.5 — both decelerating from prior readings of 8.4% and 58.9 respectively — describes an economy that is still expanding but losing altitude. Core sector at 2.3% YoY, the lowest in 18 months, is the more honest read of physical output: cement, steel, and electricity generation do not lie the way deflators can. GST at ₹2,00,640 cr confirms consumption is holding, but the split between PV sales at +26.1% and e-commerce GMV growth at 12.4% (halved from 25%) maps a two-speed economy — affluent and accelerating at the top, softening in the middle.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US GDP SAAR at 1.5% — down from 2.1% — while S&P 500 sits at a 100th-percentile 7,718 is the central contradiction in global markets today. US 10Y at 4.77% (86th percentile) has risen four of the last five periods — the bond market is pricing higher-for-longer while equities price a soft landing — and both cannot be correct simultaneously. Brent at $96.28 (up four of five sessions from $88.10) adds a commodity inflation overlay that the Fed, with core PCE still at 3.34%, cannot ignore; US VIX at a 8th-percentile 14.53 suggests markets have not begun to price the resolution of this contradiction.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

FII equity net flows turned negative at -₹114 cr — a sharp reversal from +₹22,615 cr prior — while DII absorption at ₹128 cr is at a 22nd-percentile low, meaning domestic institutions are not stepping in with conviction. SIP inflows at ₹29,845 cr remain at the 85th percentile, but SIP account growth at 1.55% MoM (a 2nd-percentile pace) confirms that incremental flows are coming from larger tickets, not new participants — a structurally narrower base than the headline suggests. Corporate bond issuance at ₹1,12,000 cr (7th percentile) signals that firms are accessing capital markets aggressively, likely anticipating that bank credit — constrained by a 83.04% CD ratio — will become more expensive or less available.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Nifty 50 at 23,897 has fallen five consecutive sessions from 24,208, while Bank Nifty at 57,369 (95th percentile) holds near its highs — a divergence that is difficult to sustain if CD ratio pressure translates into NIM compression and risk-weight tightening. Retail mall vacancy at a 15th-percentile 6.7% — tightest in three years — and office absorption at 26.9 mn sqft (driven by GCCs, not traditional IT) tell a real estate story that is bifurcated by asset class: commercial and experiential retail are tight, while residential launches at a 0th-percentile 106,000 units and an affordability index at a 19th-percentile 3.5 signal that the housing market is pricing out the mass buyer. REIT prices — Embassy down to ₹369 from ₹438, Mindspace to ₹345 from ₹501 — suggest the office absorption story is not yet translating into investor returns.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three risks, ranked by probability × impact: First, Brent sustaining above $95 — already at $96.28 for four consecutive sessions — pushes fuel CPI from -3.78% to positive within 60 days, takes headline CPI above 4%, and eliminates any residual case for a rate cut while widening CAD by approximately 40bps per $10 move. Second, CD ratio at 83.04% triggering a macro-prudential response — risk-weight increases on unsecured or NBFC lending — which would compress NBFC credit growth (already down from 17% to 13%) and reprice the mid-cap financials that dominate active fund portfolios. Third, US 10Y at 4.77% with VIX at 14.53 (8th percentile) is the classic setup for a volatility event — if the Fed signals higher-for-longer more forcefully, carry unwinds hit INR and FII flows simultaneously, testing RBI's reserve management. Watch Thursday's US CPI print: a surprise above 3.5% is the single data point most likely to detonate all three risks in sequence.

"}
